Indicator 4: Number of people reached through social media (excluding Instagram stories, LinkedIn and Twitter). Target: 900.000 people.

actual.value: 883.226 people were reached through social media. This number covers both organic and paid efforts. Furthermore, 16 celebrities and influencers shared content and videos via Instagram, Facebook and Twitter reaching around 274.000 followers, all of whom potentially have gained knowledge about the Peru-project and Operation Dagsværk

title.narrative: Output 2.1: Weekend training camps.
Indicator 1: Number of students being trained - all of whom were subsequently supposed to do campaign activities at their respective schools. Target: 55 students.

target.value: 55 students participating in the training camps.

actual.value: Due to covid, the weekend training camp set up were cancelled and rescheduled taking form as a tour instead. This meant meeting and training the students in smaller groups instead of a collective training camp. However, it is estimated that around 51-68 students participated in the renewed training.

title.narrative: Output 2.5: Selling postcards.
Indicator 5: Number of schools selling postcards on the day of Operation Dagsværk. Target: 35 schools.

target.value: No targets or results in year 1.

actual.value: No targets or results in year 1.

Only 7 of the 35 participating schools ended up selling postcards. Because of covid and the limited possibility of working closely together due to the risk of infecting one another, we came up with the possibility for the students to sell postcards (via e-mail, phone etc.) as a way of participating. Initially, several schools were interested in this possibility, however the support slowly fell when several schools withdrew from the project.
